title: A plan that waited past its pleasure

captions.physics: Preparing conditions for leisure in advance
captions.energy: Keeping desire in a suspended state

meaning: Shared leisure becomes fragile when prepared pleasure waits too long for permission to begin and then meets an ordinary obstacle.
text: A well arranged pleasure can be postponed too long. The Emperor in the physical position of Svadhisthana describes organisation: preparing a place, choosing a time and establishing an understandable order. The Hanged Man in energy leans towards leaving desire suspended, reconsidering conditions instead of beginning. The Tower in emotions makes a broken expectation keenly felt. If the plan fails, the whole promised evening seems lost. Prepared action, a delaying motive and shock belong to different aspects of leisure. Waiting itself can give a small opportunity the weight of a large promise.

For example, you prepare somewhere to watch the evening sky. Everything is ready, but leaving waits for a small task, then for more beautiful light. By the time you set out, clouds cover the sky. **Pleasure struggles to live when assigned an ever more suitable moment.** Disappointment is understandable, and the missed participation makes it heavier. Going out together could have been pleasant before the imagined best hour.

The difficulty is answering the setback with a stricter plan. Every obstacle must now be excluded beforehand, so leisure waits again for complete readiness. Trying to protect desire, you give it less real space. A pause helps when it opens another way to participate. A sufficiently suitable moment can offer more living pleasure than an ideal condition that remains forever anticipated.
